summary: Evaluate the laboratory-frame neutron kinetic energy of D(d,n)3He from two deuteron velocities and a detector line-of-sight unit vector, in non-relativistic two-body kinematics. The call returns the energy in keV and nothing else. Three corrections are applied to the retained route: its non-positive fallback is removed, so a lab energy of zero is returned as zero rather than as the 2450 keV centre-of-mass partition; the relation is evaluated in an algebraically equivalent regrouping whose two terms are each non-negative for every physical input, so the result cannot round below zero and no clamp is applied; and a finite input whose arithmetic double precision cannot represent is rejected rather than returned as a non-finite value or silently as zero.

identity.relation: two deuteron velocities and a detector direction to the laboratory-frame neutron energy of the D(d,n)3He reaction
identity.definition: Forms the centre-of-mass velocity (v1 + v2)/2 and the relative velocity v1 - v2, adds the DD Q value to the relative kinetic energy of the reduced mass to get E_avail, partitions E_avail by the neutron/He-3 mass ratio to get E_cm, forms the boost E_boost from the centre-of-mass speed, bounds the direction cosine c = v_cm_hat . d_hat to [-1, 1], and returns (sqrt(E_cm) - sqrt(E_boost))^2 + 2*sqrt(E_cm*E_boost)*(1 + c), all in keV. The regrouping is algebraically identical to the retained route's E_cm + E_boost + 2*sqrt(E_cm*E_boost)*c. No angular weighting is applied.
identity.model: non-relativistic two-body kinematics with a fixed Q value; no anisotropy factor
identity.geometry: the detector vector is a direction from the reaction point to the detector, in the same Cartesian frame as the velocities
identity.coordinates: three-component Cartesian vectors; no frame transformation is performed
identity.boundary: stationary reactants collapse the boost to zero and the result to the mass-partition energy 2450.47589941598 keV; the returned value is non-negative for every accepted input because both terms of the evaluated form are individually non-negative -- a square, and a product of non-negative factors since c is bounded to [-1, 1] -- so no clamp is applied and no value is replaced by zero; at the complete-cancellation configuration, where E_cm and E_boost are the same double and the detector is exactly backward, both terms are exactly zero and the returned energy is exactly 0.0
assumptions: The reaction is the two-body D(d,n)3He channel with Q = 3.27 MeV, and the reactants are non-relativistic.
The two deuterons are distinguishable and their order is immaterial to the result.

The detector vector is a unit vector; it is used directly as a direction and is rejected rather than normalised when it is not. Because the norm is accepted within an absolute tolerance of 1e-12, an accepted detector can have a norm slightly above one, which is why the direction cosine is bounded before use.

The angular weight is 1.0 and is not returned: this asset computes the unnormalised two-body energy. Angular weighting is a separate capability that this asset does not provide, does not import and does not compose; no public SciRel callable for it exists at this development baseline.

E_lab = (sqrt(E_cm) ± sqrt(E_boost))^2 at the two extreme detector directions, and E_lab = (sqrt(E_cm) - sqrt(E_boost))^2 + 2*sqrt(E_cm*E_boost)*(1 + c) in general. Both terms of the general form are non-negative for c in [-1, 1], which is why the value is non-negative in exact arithmetic, why the retained route's non-positive guard has no negative physical value to protect against, and why no clamp is needed.

The relation is evaluated in double precision. A finite velocity pair whose arithmetic is not representable in double precision -- an overflowing centre-of-mass speed, an overflowing relative kinetic energy, or an overflowing product of the two energy terms -- is outside the evaluated domain and is rejected rather than approximated.

inputs.name: reactant1_velocity_cm_s
inputs.description: First deuteron velocity in the laboratory frame.
inputs.constraints: Finite and exactly three components. A finite value so large that the relation's arithmetic overflows is accepted by this constraint and rejected by the runtime representability check; no magnitude bound is imposed here.

inputs.name: reactant2_velocity_cm_s
inputs.description: Second deuteron velocity in the laboratory frame.
inputs.constraints: Finite and exactly three components. A finite value so large that the relation's arithmetic overflows is accepted by this constraint and rejected by the runtime representability check; no magnitude bound is imposed here.

inputs.name: detector_unit_vector
inputs.description: Line-of-sight direction from the reaction point to the detector.
inputs.constraints: Finite, exactly three components, and of unit Euclidean norm within an absolute tolerance of 1e-12. A non-unit vector is rejected rather than normalised. A vector whose norm is accepted but exceeds one is not rejected; its direction cosine contribution is bounded instead.

outputs.name: neutron_energy_kev
outputs.constraints: A Python float, always finite and always non-negative. The direction cosine is bounded to [-1, 1] before the sum is formed, and the evaluated form is the sum of the square (sqrt(E_cm) - sqrt(E_boost))^2 and the product 2*sqrt(E_cm*E_boost)*(1 + c), both of which are non-negative for every accepted input, so a negative cannot be produced and no clamp is applied. The value is exactly 0.0 at the complete-cancellation configuration and is strictly positive at the 8000 other doubles within +-4000 ulp of that speed, including the 997 at which the retained ordering rounds negative.

preconditions: The two deuterons are at the same spatial point and the reaction is the two-body D(d,n)3He channel.
The detector direction is expressed in the same frame as the two velocities.
The caller does not expect angular weighting from this asset.
The supplied velocities are finite and the relation's arithmetic is representable in double precision for them.
supported: Arbitrary non-relativistic deuteron velocities, including stationary and counter-streaming pairs.
Any detector direction, including the exact backward direction where the lab energy is zero.
The exact-cancellation configuration, where E_cm and E_boost are the same double and the detector is exactly backward; the returned value is exactly 0.0 rather than a rounding residue.
A detector vector accepted by the 1e-12 norm tolerance on either side of unit norm, with the direction cosine bounded rather than the input rejected.
Velocities that are large but whose arithmetic is representable, including speeds well outside the non-relativistic regime; no speed cutoff is imposed.
excluded: The Brown-Jarmie or any other angular distribution; the anisotropy factor is a separate capability that is not composed here and for which no public SciRel callable exists at this baseline.
Any treatment of the emitted neutron's subsequent transport or scattering.
Velocity pairs whose arithmetic overflows double precision; these raise rather than being approximated or reported as a non-finite value.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when a velocity vector or the detector vector is not finite or is not exactly three components, and when the detector vector's Euclidean norm differs from 1 by more than an absolute tolerance of 1e-12. The shape check is applied before the norm check.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError when the relation's arithmetic is not representable in double precision for the supplied finite velocities. Every intermediate and the returned value is checked for finiteness: the centre-of-mass and relative velocities, the available, centre-of-mass and boost energies, the direction cosine, and the energy in both MeV and keV. Two signatures are pinned by tests, both with finite inputs: two 1.0e308 cm/s velocities, where v1 + v2 overflows and the direction cosine is NaN, and a single 1.0e150 cm/s velocity, where the boost overflows while the centre-of-mass energy stays finite. The check is on representability and not a speed cutoff: no magnitude threshold is introduced, and a large but representable velocity is evaluated and returned. The retained route's non-positive substitution is removed, so a computed value near zero is returned rather than replaced by the centre-of-mass energy.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this operator has no iteration or feedback.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no value, and a call that fails the representability check produces no partial energy.

provenance.lineage_summary: SciRel-owned formalisation of the retained FIDASIM L1 route DD中子运动学能量, anchored by that bundle on src/fidasim.f90:11082-11176 (get_dd_neutron_energy). The bundle is a source-free formalisation: this run did not read FIDASIM Fortran and the anchor line numbers are the bundle's, not independently verified. The relation, its constants and its input contract are carried from the retained route unchanged. This candidate is derived from the V4 review unit of the same name, which is derived from the V3 and V2 units of the same name. The V2 unit's finding that the non-positive fallback was algebraically unreachable was shown false by V3 and is kept here: the guard fires on 6983 of the 8001 doubles neighbouring the exact-cancellation speed, of which 997 are strictly negative rounding artifacts. V4 kept that removal and answered the retained ordering's negative with an empirical max(0.0, value) clamp; V5 removes the clamp and replaces the evaluated ordering with an algebraically equivalent regrouping into two non-negative terms, so the non-negativity is structural rather than imposed, and adds a fail-closed representability check on the finite inputs for which the arithmetic overflows. The bundle states no licence and cites no reference for its constants.

example.description: Confirm the stationary mass-partition anchor, the forward-over-reverse ordering, the values at the two V4 cancellation witnesses, the exact zero at the complete-cancellation configuration, the bound on a detector accepted at the norm tolerance boundary, the detector unit-norm rejection, and the rejection of a finite velocity whose arithmetic overflows.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.fusion import calculate_dd_neutron_lab_energy_kev
FORWARD = (1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
stationary = calculate_dd_neutron_lab_energy_kev(
    reactant1_velocity_cm_s=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
    reactant2_velocity_cm_s=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
    detector_unit_vector=FORWARD)
assert stationary == 2450.47589941598
forward = calculate_dd_neutron_lab_energy_kev(
    reactant1_velocity_cm_s=(1.0e8, 0.0, 0.0),
    reactant2_velocity_cm_s=(5.0e7, 0.0, 0.0),
    detector_unit_vector=FORWARD)
reverse = calculate_dd_neutron_lab_energy_kev(
    reactant1_velocity_cm_s=(1.0e8, 0.0, 0.0),
    reactant2_velocity_cm_s=(5.0e7, 0.0, 0.0),
    detector_unit_vector=(-1.0, 0.0, 0.0))
assert forward > reverse > 0.0
# The neutron emitted backwards near the speed that brings it to rest in the
# lab.  The retained route substitutes 2450.47589941598 keV at both of these
# speeds; here the value is zero to the precision of the arithmetic.
for speed, expected in ((2165199149.095274, 2.9996435921028974e-25),
                        (2165199149.0952773, 2.2132478772107012e-25)):
    witness = np.array([-speed, 0.0, 0.0])
    value = calculate_dd_neutron_lab_energy_kev(
        reactant1_velocity_cm_s=witness,
        reactant2_velocity_cm_s=witness,
        detector_unit_vector=FORWARD)
    assert value == expected and 0.0 < value < 1.0e-24
# The complete-cancellation configuration: E_boost equals E_cm to the last bit
# and the detector is exactly backward, so both terms vanish exactly.
exact = np.array([-2165199149.095298, 0.0, 0.0])
assert calculate_dd_neutron_lab_energy_kev(
    reactant1_velocity_cm_s=exact,
    reactant2_velocity_cm_s=exact,
    detector_unit_vector=FORWARD) == 0.0
# A detector accepted by the 1e-12 norm tolerance on the high side.
boundary = (1.0 + 1.0e-13, 0.0, 0.0)
assert calculate_dd_neutron_lab_energy_kev(
    reactant1_velocity_cm_s=(1.0e8, 0.0, 0.0),
    reactant2_velocity_cm_s=(5.0e7, 0.0, 0.0),
    detector_unit_vector=boundary) == calculate_dd_neutron_lab_energy_kev(
    reactant1_velocity_cm_s=(1.0e8, 0.0, 0.0),
    reactant2_velocity_cm_s=(5.0e7, 0.0, 0.0),
    detector_unit_vector=FORWARD)
try:
    calculate_dd_neutron_lab_energy_kev(
        reactant1_velocity_cm_s=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
        reactant2_velocity_cm_s=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
        detector_unit_vector=(2.0, 0.0, 0.0))
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('a non-unit detector must be rejected')
# Two finite 1e308 cm/s velocities: v1 + v2 overflows, so the arithmetic is not
# representable.  V4's clamp answered this with 0.0; it is rejected here.
big = np.array([1.0e308, 0.0, 0.0])
try:
    calculate_dd_neutron_lab_energy_kev(
        reactant1_velocity_cm_s=big,
        reactant2_velocity_cm_s=big,
        detector_unit_vector=FORWARD)
except ValueError as error:
    assert 'not representable' in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError('an overflowing velocity must be rejected')
example.expected: 2450.47589941598 keV for stationary reactants, matching the retained route's own anchor; a strictly larger energy for a forward detector than for a backward one, both positive; 2.9996435921028974e-25 and 2.2132478772107012e-25 keV at the two V4 cancellation witnesses, where the retained route substitutes 2450.47589941598 keV and where V3 returned -8.881784197001252e-13 keV at the second, and where V4 returned exactly 0.0 by clamping; exactly 0.0 at the complete-cancellation configuration, where the retained route substitutes 2450.47589941598 keV; a result for the tolerance-boundary detector identical to the same call with an exactly unit detector, where the retained route returns a larger value; a ValueError for a non-unit detector vector; and a ValueError for two finite 1e308 cm/s velocities, where V4 returned 0.0.

scope: How this evidence is organised. The frozen V5 review established every claim below by comparing this asset against external arms -- the retained source route and the frozen V2, V3 and V4 candidates -- which live outside this repository and are reachable only in the review environment. The maintained tests in this repository replay none of those comparisons and depend on no source checkout, no candidate directory and no L1 payload. They protect the claims that are self-contained: the public relation's own runtime behaviour at pinned witnesses, its input and failure contracts, and its regression values. Where a claim rests on an external comparison it is recorded here as the frozen review's finding and is marked as not replayed by the maintained tests.

How this evidence is organised (2/2). The maintained suite is tests/operator_contracts/test_dd_neutron_lab_energy.py, and it is self-contained: it re-derives E_cm, E_boost and the direction cosine from the constants this asset publishes, so its assertions are independent of the asset's own evaluation order, and it imports nothing outside SciRel, NumPy and pytest.

The removal of the non-positive fallback. Frozen review finding: the retained route and the frozen predecessors substitute the centre-of-mass energy at the two pinned witnesses. Not replayed by the maintained tests, which cannot reach those arms. Protected here: at those two speeds the public callable returns 2.9996435921028974e-25 and 2.2132478772107012e-25 keV, strictly positive and twenty-two orders of magnitude below the relation's scale, and not the 2450.47589941598 keV the removed fallback produced.

The reachability of the removed branch. Frozen review finding: the fallback fired on 6983 of the 8001 doubles within +-4000 ulp of the exact-cancellation speed, 997 of them on a strictly negative value, against the V2 review's finding that the branch could not be reached. Not replayed by the maintained tests, which cannot reach the removed route. Recorded here because it is the reason for the removal.

No clamp is applied. Protected by the maintained tests as a census over the same 8001 doubles: exactly one returns 0.0 -- the single double at which E_boost equals E_cm to the last bit -- and the other 8000 are strictly positive, none negative. A clamp would have answered every non-positive value with zero instead.

The exactness of the zero at the complete-cancellation configuration, in both lab-frame sign conventions. Protected by the maintained tests, which re-derive that E_cm equals E_boost to the last bit at that speed and that the direction cosine is exactly -1, so both terms of the evaluated form are exactly zero.

The rounding bound that replaces bit-identity with the retained ordering. Protected by the maintained tests: the difference from the ordering E_cm + E_boost + 2*sqrt(E_cm*E_boost)*c, re-derived from the published constants, stays within 8 units in the last place of E_cm + E_boost over 840 inputs from 1e6 to 1e10 cm/s. Frozen review measurement: no more than 5.16 over the same sample.

The fail-closed representability check. Frozen review finding: the two finite 1e308 cm/s witness returned 0.0 from V4 because max(0.0, NaN) is 0.0, and a finite 1e150 cm/s velocity returned positive infinity because max(0.0, inf) is inf. Not replayed by the maintained tests, which cannot reach V4. Protected here: both inputs raise ValueError from the public callable, naming the intermediate that was not finite.

That no speed cutoff is invented. Protected by the maintained tests: representable velocities from 1e6 to 1e10 cm/s are evaluated and returned, including speeds far outside the non-relativistic regime, and the representability check is read from the compiled code object to confirm it is a finiteness test with no magnitude comparison and no literal bound.

The direction-cosine bound. Frozen review finding: a detector of norm 1 + 1e-13 is accepted by the retained route's own norm tolerance and inflates its result and V3's. Not replayed by the maintained tests. Protected here: at that detector the public callable returns exactly the unit-detector value, the unbounded dot product is confirmed to exceed one, and the inflated value it would otherwise produce is shown to exceed the bounded result.

The retained route's own anchors, re-derived rather than compared. Protected by the maintained tests: the stationary mass-partition energy 1000 * m_He3 * Q / (m_n + m_He3) equals 2450.47589941598 keV and is what the public callable returns for stationary reactants, and the forward detector exceeds the reverse one on the retained route's own inputs.

The two-body square-root bracket, E_lab = (sqrt(E_cm) +- sqrt(E_boost))^2 at the two extremes, which is why the value is non-negative in exact arithmetic. Protected by the maintained tests against the bracket re-derived from the published constants, to a bound rather than bit-wise because the two forms round differently.

The input contract: shape rejection, rejection of a non-unit detector rather than normalisation, the absolute 1e-12 norm tolerance boundary, rejection of a non-finite component by the input contract rather than by the representability check, and the keyword-only calling convention. All protected by the maintained tests directly against the public callable.

That the anisotropy capability is not composed into this asset and no angular weight is returned. Protected by the maintained tests: the module exposes no angular_weight, and no anisotropy module is loaded by a call.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Establishes, on the frozen review's external comparison, the retained route's two-body lab-energy relation, its input contract, the behaviour and reachability of the non-positive branch it removes, and the rounding bound against the retained ordering. Establishes, on the maintained self-contained tests, the non-negativity of the returned value by construction, the exactness of the zero at the complete-cancellation configuration, the census showing no clamp is applied, and the failure of non-representable arithmetic. The maintained tests depend on no source checkout, candidate directory or L1 payload. This asset does not establish the accuracy of the non-relativistic approximation at any energy, does not establish the mass constants, the atomic mass unit or the MeV-per-joule factor against any independent measurement, and does not establish that the source's Fortran implements this expression, since the retained bundle is source-free.
known_limitations: The reformulation is a change of evaluation order and not a change of relation, so the returned energy is no longer bit-identical to the retained route. The difference is asserted within a measured rounding bound of 8 units in the last place of E_cm + E_boost, but that bound is an assertion over the sampled input scales rather than a proof over the whole accepted domain.

The returned value is no longer exactly 0.0 at the two speeds V4 pinned: it is 2.9996435921028974e-25 and 2.2132478772107012e-25 keV, because E_cm and E_boost differ by one and three units in the last place there. Both are twenty-two orders of magnitude below the 1 keV scale of the relation, and neither is negative, but a caller that compared against an exact zero at those two inputs would see a change.

Non-negativity is structural for the evaluated form, but the terms E_cm and E_boost are themselves rounded. The guarantee is that the returned value cannot be negative, not that it is the correctly rounded value of the exact relation.

The representability check rejects a finite input whose arithmetic overflows, but it does not establish where the non-relativistic approximation stops being scientifically meaningful. That boundary remains a physical statement about the relation and is not enforced by a magnitude threshold.
The mass constants, the atomic mass unit and the MeV-per-joule factor are carried from the retained route unverified. The bundle cites no reference and states no licence for them.
The Q value is fixed at 3.27 MeV; no excitation or channel competition is modelled.
No angular weighting is applied. A caller that multiplies the returned energy by an angular factor is applying a distribution this asset does not own.
The detector unit-norm precondition is enforced rather than relaxed, so a caller holding a slightly non-unit line-of-sight vector must normalise it first.

The single unit test that sweeps the +-4000 ulp neighbourhood takes about 27 seconds, because the relation is evaluated 8001 times. The frozen review measured the same band on three arms at once; the maintained test evaluates only this asset.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.

The frozen V5 review's comparisons against the retained route and the frozen V2, V3 and V4 candidates are not replayable from this repository: those arms live outside it, and the maintained tests neither reach them nor depend on them. The claims they established are recorded in this document's verification scope and marked as not replayed; a reviewer who needs to re-check them must return to the frozen review environment. The maintained tests protect the self-contained subset, and no public test requires an external checkout.
